question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) if a sum of ₹400 is borrowed for 5.5 years at 12% per annum rate of interest.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective Rate of Interest = Rate × Time

Effective Rate = 12% × 5.5 = 66%

Simple Interest = 66% of Principal

SI = 66% of 400 = 66 × 4 = 264

**∴ The correct answer is ₹264.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹400

Rate (R) = 12% per annum

Time (T) = 5.5 years

 
 Rate = 12% p.a. | Time = 5.5 years
 
 P
 ₹400
 
 SI
 ₹?
 

 

 Interest accumulates linearly
 SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (400 × 12 × 5.5) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 4 × 12 × 5.5

⇒ SI = 48 × 5.5

⇒ SI = 264

**∴ The correct answer is ₹264.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount (A) received after time T is given by the formula: A = P + SI = P × (1 + RT ÷ 100).

Difference Between SI and CI (2 years)

For a principal P and rate R, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest over exactly 2 years is calculated directly as: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Rule of 72

A quick trick to estimate the number of years required to double your invested money at a given fixed annual interest rate is to divide 72 by the interest rate (R).
